name: HTTP APIs
tagline: Any REST, GraphQL or MCP API described once as a YAML plugin: routes, state, answers, callbacks and failures on cue.
point: https://<provider host>:8443 with the Stuntman Test CA trusted

capabilities.title: Routes as readable steps
capabilities.text: Each route reads receive, let, keep, wait, decide, respond, send. Edit in the route editor or the YAML; every change is validated first.

capabilities.title: State and data tables
capabilities.text: keep stores what the provider remembers between calls; data tables (people, flagged documents) feed answers through lookup().

capabilities.title: Auth like the provider
capabilities.text: OAuth2 client credentials with a token route, Basic, session cookies from a login route, and mTLS client certificates.

capabilities.title: Browser steps
capabilities.text: Plugins draw authorize pages (PKCE, OTP, pick a person) and push approvals the app polls. Agents pass them with authorize_as and approve_push.

capabilities.title: GraphQL and streams
capabilities.text: Routes share POST /graphql and answer by operation name. Answers can stream as SSE, NDJSON or plain chunks.

capabilities.title: Be an MCP server
capabilities.text: An mcp: block serves tools/list and tools/call on /<service>/mcp; each tool decides like a route. set_mcp_tool adds one.

capabilities.title: Signed webhooks
capabilities.text: send steps sign as hex HMAC, Stripe, Svix, GitHub or CloudEvents. Delays follow the environment's clock: advance_clock(by="30d").

capabilities.title: Idempotency and scenarios
capabilities.text: A repeated Idempotency-Key replays the first answer (409 on another body). Scenarios switch a service's behaviour by name.

capabilities.title: Catch unmatched calls
capabilities.text: Requests no route takes are kept with the closest route; route_from_request drafts the missing route from one.

excerpts.title: A route, step by step, with its YAML

callouts.title: Routes of the plugin
callouts.text: One route per kind of request the provider takes, with its calls today and billing.

callouts.title: Receive
callouts.text: Bearer token from the plugin's own token route; a missing body field answers 400 like the provider.

callouts.title: Keep
callouts.text: State the provider remembers between calls, keyed by an expression. Refused calls change nothing.

callouts.title: Decide
callouts.text: First match wins: conditions on body, state and data pick a named answer.

callouts.title: The same file
callouts.text: The YAML beside the editor marks the changed lines. Try it runs a sample request without keeping anything.

excerpts.title: A browser step the plugin draws

callouts.title: People from the plugin
callouts.text: Synthetic people with their certificates come from the plugin's data table.

callouts.title: Broken on purpose
callouts.text: Pick a person whose certificate expired to see how the app handles it.

callouts.title: One-time code
callouts.text: Any 6 digits pass; 000000 is refused on purpose.

callouts.title: Authorize or Deny
callouts.text: Redirects to the app with code and state; the token call then checks the PKCE verifier.

callouts.title: What Stuntman records
callouts.text: Each step lands on the timeline. Agents skip the page with authorize_as.

excerpts.title: Webhook signing, idempotency and the clock

callouts.title: Sign like the provider
callouts.text: Hex HMAC, hex with timestamp, Stripe, Svix, GitHub or CloudEvents, with the secret and header the app checks.

callouts.title: Break every send
callouts.text: Wrong signature, old timestamp, no signature, sent twice or out of order, until set back to none.

callouts.title: Idempotency-Key
callouts.text: The same key gets the first answer again with no webhook; the same key with another body gets 409.

callouts.title: The environment's clock
callouts.text: Move it 1 h, 1 day or 30 days: waiting webhooks go out and now() follows. Back to real time resets it.

provoke.name: Any named answer
provoke.what: The next N calls (or the next 10 minutes) get a declined, expired or not-found answer

provoke.name: Network failures
provoke.what: Connection reset, empty reply or a timeout

provoke.name: HTML error page
provoke.what: A 200 whose body is an HTML error page, as a proxy in front of the provider sends

provoke.name: Expired tokens
provoke.what: Every token and session cookie becomes invalid; the next call gets 401

provoke.name: Rate limit
provoke.what: Calls above the rate get 429 with Retry-After

provoke.name: A share of failures
provoke.what: A random share of calls fails

provoke.name: Slow provider
provoke.what: Every answer waits a range of latency

provoke.name: Broken stream
provoke.what: Half the parts then a dropped connection, or 2 s more per part

provoke.name: MCP session expired
provoke.what: The next MCP request gets 404 and the client must start a new session

provoke.name: Bad webhooks
provoke.what: Wrong signature, old timestamp, unsigned, sent twice or out of order

provoke.name: Person says no
provoke.what: The authorize page is denied, or the push approval is rejected or times out

advantages.title: Failures the sandbox lacks
advantages.text: A sandbox rarely times out on the third call or sends a webhook twice. Stuntman does it on the next call, then stops by itself.

advantages.title: Days pass in seconds
advantages.text: A 30-day renewal webhook goes out when you move the environment's clock, not next month.

advantages.title: No keys, no quota
advantages.text: Calls never leave the machine. Billing is a counter that points at retry loops, never real money.

advantages.title: Every call explained
advantages.text: Each call leaves a sentence, the answer name and the steps it took, readable by people and by agents.

notes: Expressions are a side-effect-free CEL-like subset: a plugin cannot reach the network or the disk unless it declares it.
The clock belongs to HTTP plugins; tokens, links and the other built-in lines keep real time.
